description: MCP Tasks (spec/command-metadata.md, "Tasks"; MCP 2026-07-28 SEP-2663) against a backend where todo-create-batch declares task: "optional". Each case names the client it needs: "tasks" declares the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks capability on MCP 2026-07-28 and expects todo-create-batch to return a task polled via tasks/get to completion; "no-tasks" declares no tasks capability and expects todo-create-batch to run inline. For TypeScript, Python and Rust backends, dx/run-conformance.ts also runs post-completion retention and execution run-budget timeout checks against todo-slow-task (TASK_CONFORMANCE=1). Cases may read the task's wire messages under "$task": "$task.answer" is the task answer to tools/call, "$task.get" the tasks/get answer that settled it and "$task.answeredMs" how long the task answer took to arrive. The Claude Code cases check what Claude Code's task client requires (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#mcp-tasks-for-server-authors, read 2026-11-26). Its rule that a failed task carries error.message cannot be reached from a command: a failed CommandResult is a completed task with isError, and failed is kept for internal errors, so each language's task unit tests cover it.

tests.name: afd-detail reports task: optional on todo-create-batch
tests.description: Discovery metadata advertises task: optional on todo-create-batch and omits task on todo-create

tests.name: Batch create runs as a task for a tasks-capable client
tests.description: todo-create-batch starts a task, polls tasks/get to completed, and persists the todos

tests.name: Non-task commands still run inline for a tasks-capable client
tests.description: todo-create has default task: never and executes inline even when the client declares tasks

tests.name: Batch create runs inline when client does not declare tasks
tests.description: todo-create-batch has task: optional so a client without io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks gets an inline result

tests.name: Claude Code: the task answer carries every field its client requires
tests.description: Claude Code's task client needs resultType "task", a taskId of at most 128 printable ASCII characters with no spaces, a status, createdAt, lastUpdatedAt and ttlMs (the tasks extension) and pollIntervalMs, which it clamps to 250-30000

tests.name: Claude Code: tasks/get answers carry every field its client requires
tests.description: Claude Code polls tasks/get and needs resultType "complete", taskId, status, createdAt, lastUpdatedAt and ttlMs in each answer, and reads the outcome from the completed task's result

tests.name: Claude Code: the task answer does not wait for the work, and a working poll carries every field
tests.description: Claude Code expects the task answer at once and the work after it (over HTTP, within its per-request timer). A task that sleeps 3000 ms answers while it is still working, well inside the sleep (the runner times the answer with a monotonic clock over stdio), and Claude Code's first tasks/get, while it still works, carries resultType "complete", taskId, status, createdAt, lastUpdatedAt and ttlMs. The answer arriving before the sleep ends shows the server did not wait for the work; it cannot show the handler had not yet started

tests.name: Claude Code: a failed task carries error.message
tests.description: Claude Code tells the model a failed task's error.message. AFD fails a task only for an internal error: here a result JSON cannot hold (a BigInt in TypeScript, a cycle in Python). Rust's results are always JSON, so its failed shape is unit-tested in packages/rust/tests/server_tasks.rs
